target.title: fix(control-ui): show unavailable sizes for negative byte counts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a narrow Control UI display bug where an invalid negative byte metric could still be formatted as if it were a real byte size.

The affected helper is `formatBytes()` in `ui/src/lib/agents/display.ts`. It already treats missing values and non-finite numbers as unavailable, but finite negative values previously passed through to the shared `formatByteSize()` formatter. Since byte counts represent cardinal quantities, a value like `-1` is not a meaningful UI size and should use the same unavailable marker as other invalid inputs.

In practice, this means Control UI status details could show a misleading negative size label instead of the existing `-` fallback when upstream/runtime data provides a malformed or sentinel-like negative byte count.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix keeps the behavior at the Control UI display boundary. The shared `formatByteSize()` helper remains a generic formatter for caller-provided numbers; this PR only tightens the wrapper that decides whether a byte metric is displayable in the UI.

Core production diff:

```diff
 export function formatBytes(bytes?: number) {
-  if (bytes == null || !Number.isFinite(bytes)) {
+  if (bytes == null || !Number.isFinite(bytes) || bytes < 0) {
     return "-";
   }
```

This intentionally preserves the existing formatting contract for valid values:

```text
undefined -> -
-1        -> -
0         -> 0 B
512       -> 512 B
1536      -> 1.5 KB
```

The colocated regression test adds the missing negative-input assertion while keeping the existing positive formatting assertions unchanged.

## User Impact

Users now see the unavailable marker `-` when Control UI receives an invalid negative byte count, rather than a negative byte-size label that looks like a valid measurement.

The visible effect is intentionally small and defensive: normal zero and positive byte displays continue to render exactly as before, while malformed negative metrics are no longer presented as meaningful sizes.

## Evidence

### Real Behavior Proof

This PR includes after-fix terminal proof from the current branch source, not only a unit-test claim. The temporary local script reads `ui/src/lib/agents/display.ts`, evaluates the exported `formatBytes()` function body from this PR, and imports the real shared formatter from `packages/normalization-core/src/format.ts`.

Observed output:

```text
Control UI byte formatter after-fix proof (current branch source)
formatBytes source: ui/src/lib/agents/display.ts
formatByteSize source: packages/normalization-core/src/format.ts
guard line: if (bytes == null || !Number.isFinite(bytes) || bytes < 0) {
formatBytes(-1): -
formatBytes(0): 0 B
formatBytes(512): 512 B
formatBytes(1536): 1.5 KB
```

This shows the changed runtime behavior directly: the invalid negative byte count now renders as the unavailable marker, while normal zero and positive byte formatting still renders unchanged.

GitHub validation also confirms the PR body contains acceptable real-behavior evidence:
- `Real behavior proof` passed on the current PR head

### Before/After Behavior Delta

This PR also includes direct before/after proof for the changed Control UI formatter boundary. The comparison uses `upstream/main` for the base behavior and the current PR head for the fixed behavior:

```text
Control UI byte formatter before/after proof
base source: upstream/main:ui/src/lib/agents/display.ts
head source: HEAD:ui/src/lib/agents/display.ts

base main:
formatBytes(-1): -1 B
formatBytes(0): 0 B
formatBytes(512): 512 B
formatBytes(1536): 1.5 KB

PR head:
formatBytes(-1): -
formatBytes(0): 0 B
formatBytes(512): 512 B
formatBytes(1536): 1.5 KB
```

This isolates the behavior changed by the PR: only the invalid negative byte count moves from a misleading byte-size label to the existing unavailable marker, while valid zero and positive byte counts keep the same display output.

### Regression Coverage

Focused regression coverage added:
- `formatBytes(-1)` returns `-`
- existing zero and positive byte formatting assertions remain unchanged

### Possible Call Chain / Impact

```text
Control UI status/detail data
  -> formatBytes(bytes)
  -> unavailable guard for nullish, non-finite, or negative values
  -> formatByteSize(...) only for valid zero/positive byte counts
  -> rendered byte-size label in Control UI
```

### Validation

- `git diff --check` passed
- GitHub `Real behavior proof` check passed on the current PR head
- `pnpm --dir ui test -- src/lib/agents/display.test.ts` was attempted locally, but the command ran the full UI suite and hit local environment failures unrelated to this diff: Chinese locale-formatted strings, missing Playwright Chromium, and a pre-existing Vite alias assertion. No production files outside `ui/src/lib/agents/display.ts` and `ui/src/lib/agents/display.test.ts` were changed.

AI-assisted: drafted and validated with Codex; I reviewed the change and understand the behavior.
